question: Does the geometry of transformer attention outputs explain why large sparse dictionaries waste most of their features, and can geometry-aware initialization fix that failure without an auxiliary revival loss?

key_findings.claim: Attention outputs occupy a substantially lower-dimensional empirical subspace than MLP outputs or residual streams across the tested transformer families and datasets.
key_findings.evidence: Effective rank is reported around 60% of the model dimension for attention output and around 90% for the other activation sites. Only 74.7% of attention-output singular values exceed 1% of the maximum, and 39.1% of dimensions recover more than 99% of downstream loss versus 95.3% and 96.9% for MLP and residual activations.

key_findings.claim: The learned output projection W_O further collapses the concatenated multi-head representation rather than low rank being explained solely by each head's dimensional bottleneck.
key_findings.evidence: The paper decomposes variance along output singular directions into variance supplied by concatenated heads Z and scaling by W_O. The leading spectrum follows Z, while tail suppression aligns with W_O; effective-rank comparisons of Z support the same conclusion.

key_findings.claim: Across LlamaScope autoencoders, lower effective rank is strongly associated with more dead features, and the association persists across dictionary sizes and target sparsities.
key_findings.evidence: Layerwise attention outputs align visually with high dead-feature counts in Figure 5. In Appendix F, for L0=32 and 65,536 features, attention sites have 78.81%-94.02% dead features while two of three residual sites have 1.35% or less; the pattern remains across L0 values 32, 64, and 128.

key_findings.claim: Active Subspace Initialization projects initial SAE decoder directions into leading activation principal components and ties the encoder to their transpose.
key_findings.evidence: The method estimates V_active, applies W_D V_active V_active-transpose to the decoder initialization, and sets W_E to W_D-transpose. This changes only initialization and adds no recurring loss or compute term.

key_findings.claim: ASI improves the reconstruction-sparsity frontier and nearly eliminates feature death at 32K scale; paired with SparseAdam it remains effective up to one million features.
key_findings.evidence: For a 32,768-feature Llama-3.1-8B layer-15 SAE at L0=50, Table 4 reports 4.00 dead features, normalized MSE 0.31680, and delta LM loss 0.007847 for ASI, versus 16,144.33/0.33367/0.008375 for base TopK and 54.67/0.32241/0.007958 for AuxK. Scaling plots state that ASI plus SparseAdam reduces the 1M-feature dead rate from 87% to below 1%.

key_findings.claim: The paper establishes correlation and an effective intervention, but not a unique causal mechanism from rank collapse to feature death.
key_findings.evidence: The limitations explicitly say optimization dynamics or feature competition may mediate the correlation. Benefits are marginal at activation sites without pronounced low rank, and a fixed active dimension leaves some dead features at the lower-rank layer 7.

method.core_idea: Measure activation geometry before sparse-dictionary training and initialize decoder atoms only in the empirically active principal subspace.
method.mechanism: Singular spectra and effective-rank metrics compare attention, MLP, and residual activations. Existing LlamaScope SAEs expose the relationship with dead features. A PCA basis then projects randomly sampled decoder atoms into the top-d_init subspace, with a tied encoder; SparseAdam separately avoids stale moment estimates for inactive coordinates.
assumptions: A finite activation sample estimates the relevant principal subspace sufficiently well.
Directions with small variance are less useful for the target sparse dictionary than directions in the selected active subspace.
Dead-feature definitions based on firing frequency capture wasted capacity rather than rare but meaningful concepts.
Reconstruction error and delta language-model loss are adequate proxies for interpretability quality.

techniques.role: Quantifies dimensional collapse with singular-value entropy and loss-recovery curves.
Separates head-output variance from W_O scaling along attention-output singular directions.
Places initial dictionary atoms in leading empirical activation directions.
Updates moments only on nonzero-gradient coordinates to prevent stale momentum from reviving feature death.

evaluations.setting: Attention, MLP, and residual activations across GPT-2, Llama-3.1, Gemma-2, Qwen-3, layers, positions, and datasets.
evaluations.metric: Effective rank, singular decay, and dimensions needed to recover downstream loss.
evaluations.result: Attention outputs consistently show the lowest effective dimensionality; 39.1% of dimensions recover over 99% of downstream loss in the headline comparison.
evaluations.baseline: MLP outputs and residual-stream activations from the same models.

evaluations.setting: Llama-3.1-8B layer-15 TopK SAEs with 32,768 features across L0 values 40-80, three seeds; 15-seed significance test at L0=50.
evaluations.metric: Dead-feature count, normalized MSE, and delta LM loss.
evaluations.result: ASI has the lowest mean on all three metrics for every displayed L0; all six one-sided Welch tests against TopK and AuxK are significant, with p-values from 1.27e-6 to 2.99e-40.
evaluations.baseline: Standard TopK and TopK with the AuxK dead-feature loss.

evaluations.setting: Dictionary scaling from 16K to 1M features and extension to the Lorsa sparse attention replacement.
evaluations.metric: Reconstruction-sparsity frontier, dead-feature rate, and delta LM loss.
evaluations.result: ASI improves reconstruction at every tested scale; ASI plus SparseAdam reduces one-million-feature death below 1%, and ASI improves Lorsa under identical training hyperparameters.
evaluations.baseline: TopK, AuxK, random-subspace initialization, and standard Lorsa initialization.

limitations: Author-stated: the observed relationship between low-rank activations and dead features is correlational; its exact causal path remains unresolved.
Author-stated: ASI is most useful at clearly collapsed activation sites and gives marginal gains in near-full-rank settings.
The selected subspace dimension is a tuning choice and a fixed value does not transfer uniformly across layers with different effective ranks.
Reconstruction and delta LM loss do not directly establish that the extra live features are monosemantic, causally useful, or human-interpretable.
PCA over training activations can omit rare directions and may encode dataset-specific geometry.
failure_modes: A distribution shift can rotate the active subspace so initially well-aligned atoms become systematically misplaced.
Too small d_init may permanently exclude low-variance but behaviorally important features; too large d_init restores the random-initialization mismatch.
Optimizer staleness can reintroduce feature death at very large dictionaries even when initialization is aligned.
Treating all inactive atoms as waste can erase rare-event detectors that need much larger evaluation corpora to fire.
reusable_insights: Audit the intrinsic dimension of each activation site before choosing dictionary size or initialization.
Match model initialization support to the support of the training distribution instead of sampling isotropically in the ambient space.
Separate geometric mismatch from optimizer-state staleness with orthogonal interventions.
Report capacity utilization together with reconstruction and downstream-behavior metrics across scales.
open_questions: Can a randomized intervention that rotates or expands W_O identify whether output-projection collapse causally creates feature death?
How should d_init adapt online as a layer's activation distribution or context length changes?
Are low-variance directions semantically unimportant, or does ASI trade rare-feature coverage for average reconstruction?
Does mitigating attention-output collapse improve the transformer itself, or is that collapse a useful inductive bias?

competitive_landscape.title: Scaling and evaluating sparse autoencoders
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct SAE scaling work that develops TopK training, dead-latent mitigation, and feature-quality metrics.
competitive_landscape.difference: Gao et al. improve the sparsity objective and scale to 16M latents; this paper instead diagnoses activation geometry and changes initialization for especially collapsed attention sites.

competitive_landscape.title: Llama Scope: Extracting Millions of Features from Llama-3.1-8B with Sparse Autoencoders
competitive_landscape.relationship: Open suite of per-layer and per-sublayer Llama SAEs used as evidence in the paper's geometry/death audit.
competitive_landscape.difference: Llama Scope releases and evaluates broad SAE coverage; ASI analyzes why its attention-output dictionaries die and proposes a geometry-specific remedy.

competitive_landscape.title: On the Relationship Between Activation Outliers and Feature Death in Sparse Autoencoders
competitive_landscape.relationship: Subsequent causal account of SAE feature death based on activation-mean outliers across modalities.
competitive_landscape.difference: Simon et al. identify anti-alignment with the activation mean and eliminate that mechanism by centering; ASI emphasizes low effective rank and principal-subspace support, so the accounts make distinguishable preprocessing predictions.

competitive_landscape.title: Feature Starvation as Geometric Instability in Sparse Autoencoders
competitive_landscape.relationship: Subsequent optimization-geometric explanation and differentiable elastic-net alternative to dead-feature heuristics.
competitive_landscape.difference: That work attributes starvation to instability of amortized L1 sparse coding and modifies the objective; ASI changes only initialization to follow the data subspace and is compatible with TopK.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The authors claim the first demonstration that multi-head attention outputs are broadly low rank and that this geometry is a key cause of dead features, plus a subspace initialization that reduces one-million-feature death below 1%.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The cross-model activation-site comparison and zero-recurring-cost initialization are useful and testable. Calling low rank a cause is stronger than the evidence: later mean-centering and objective-geometry accounts supply plausible competing mechanisms that should be factorially ablated.

reviewer_notes: Read all 27 extracted pages, including the complete rank/death tables, 15-seed significance audit, cross-layer evaluation, dead-subspace analysis, and sparse-optimizer appendix. Current competing mechanisms were checked against primary arXiv pages on 2026-08-23.
